title: Design review: mixed-workload scheduler (short/long prompt-aware policy)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Schedule and run a design review for the mixed-workload scheduler prototype.
- Gather feedback/approval from Kernel team + SRE/Observability.
- Track required follow-ups before implementation + canary.

Background
Mixed short/long prompt distributions are causing head-of-line blocking (long-prefill / long-context dominating batch selection), inflating user-visible p95 tail latency (TTFT + overall). Proposal is a short/long prompt-aware policy (two-queue / class-based) with starvation prevention and guardrails.

Links
- Design doc (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/mixed-workload-scheduler-prototype-design.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-short-long-prompt-scheduling-policy.json
- Benchmark plan (draft): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/mixed-workload-benchmark-plan.json

Review scope
- Classification: short vs long (thresholds and/or predicted prefill cost), what metadata we use, and how we avoid pathological misclassification.
- Policy: two-queue dispatch; queue selection logic; aging/starvation prevention; max skew; burst caps.
- Prefill vs decode separation: where the scheduler makes decisions; what is “budgeted”; how to prevent long-prefill from dominating.
- Kernel interactions: risk of kernel auto-selection instability when mixing sequence lengths; mitigations.
- Observability: required per-class metrics/traces; dashboards; rollback triggers.
- Rollout: feature flag and config knobs; canary plan; safe parameter ramps.

Proposed meeting
- 60 minutes. Target attendees: Serving Runtime (Scheduling), Serving Runtime (Kernels), SRE/Observability, Runtime Architect reviewer.

Agenda (proposed)
1) Problem statement + success metrics (10m)
2) Proposed scheduling algorithm + guardrails (20m)
3) Prefill/decode separation and token budgeting (10m)
4) Kernel selection stability risks (10m)
5) Observability + canary guardrails (10m)

Requested reviewers
- Hiro Tanaka / Grace Kim / Yuki Sato (Kernels)
- Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant / Aisha Bello (SRE/Obs)
- Noah Patel (arch reviewer)

Acceptance criteria
- Review held with kernel + SRE representation.
- Written feedback captured + action items assigned.
- “Approved to implement behind flag” OR explicit list of blockers.
- ADR updated if material changes are required.

updates:
Meeting details
- Date/time: 2025-01-31 10:00–11:00 PT
- Facilitator: Lena Fischer
- Notes taker: Julian Moore
- Attendees: Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed, Omar El-Sayed, Julian Moore, Noah Patel, Hiro Tanaka, Grace Kim, Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Aisha Bello

Summary
- Agreement that mixed prefill dominates batch selection and causes p95/TTFT spikes under 80/20 short/long mixes.
- Two-queue policy is acceptable for prototype (simpler than SRPT), but must have explicit starvation prevention + bounded skew.
- Prefill/decode separation is required: scheduler should treat prefill as a distinct stage to prevent long-prefill monopolizing dispatch.
- Kernel team flagged a concrete risk: kernel selection instability when sequence length distribution shifts quickly (scheduler oscillation). Mitigation required before canary.

Decisions / approvals
- Approved to implement prototype behind feature flag with safe defaults.
- Must-have before canary:
  - per-class metrics + dashboards
  - starvation prevention (aging function + max wait)
  - token budget guardrails per iteration
  - mitigation for kernel auto-selection thrash (hysteresis / bucketing / pinning strategy)

Open questions
- Classification: should “short vs long” be based on prompt_tokens, total_context_tokens, or predicted prefill cost?
  - Decision: prototype supports both prompt_tokens and predicted_prefill_ms; default to prompt_tokens threshold while we validate predictor quality.
- Fairness: ensure long queue still makes progress under sustained short traffic.
  - Decision: implement aging with a max wait cap and a minimum dispatch share floor for long.

Action items
- Marcus Reed: update design doc with explicit aging function + max skew details and examples (ETA 2025-02-04).
- Omar El-Sayed: document KV-cache interaction assumptions (cache compaction/eviction under mixed workloads) and what signals to watch (ETA 2025-02-05).
- Grace Kim + Yuki Sato: propose kernel stability mitigation (seq-len bucketing or kernel selection hysteresis), add to design doc (ETA 2025-02-06).
- Julian Moore + Allison Grant: metric names/labels draft + dashboard stub list (ETA 2025-02-05).
- Sean Gallagher + Aisha Bello: draft canary rollback triggers aligned with Hosted API tail-latency SLO guardrails (ETA 2025-02-06).

Risks captured
- Risk: scheduler oscillates between classes causing kernel selection thrash and degraded throughput.
  - Mitigation: cap switching frequency; bucket seq-lens; optionally pin kernel selection per class bucket for the iteration.
- Risk: long requests starve under bursty short traffic.
  - Mitigation: aging + max wait; enforce minimum long dispatch share; add starvation counters + alerting.
